name: ClearJet

Summary: Austin-based ClearJet, an AI-enabled logistics technology startup connects shippers with unused cargo capacity on commercial flights, has raised a $25 million Edison Partners-led Series B, it tells Crunchbase News exclusively.

assessment.whatTheyDo: ClearJet is an asset-light logistics platform that books unused cargo capacity on commercial passenger flights to move e-commerce parcels faster and cheaper than traditional carriers, using AI-driven routing and (in development) AI agents to automate booking and disruption management.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Headquartered in Austin, TX — not one of the person's preferred states (CA, NY, WA, MA); no confirmed remote-hiring policy found, so some relocation friction is likely.
Founder (Chris Guggenheim) has a strong ecommerce/logistics operator background but no evident engineering background; technical depth sits with a separately-hired CTO (Jay Winters), not the founder.
The only open role found via search was a Controller (finance) position — no evidence of active senior/staff engineering hiring, which is a weaker signal per this person's stated preference.
assessment.rationale: Real applied-AI-in-logistics company with substantial evidence of a genuine, profitable, revenue-scaling product (30M+ packages/year, tripling revenue, 95-airport network) rather than a deck — a strong counter to hype-only positioning. Score is capped in the 60s rather than 80s+ because the founder isn't technical, no senior engineering roles were found advertised, and the ~50-person team plus 'hundreds of contractors' is larger/more operationally-heavy than the high-leverage small teams this person favors.
assessment.summary: ClearJet, an Austin-based logistics startup founded in 2022 by serial ecommerce entrepreneur Chris Guggenheim, raised a $25M Series B led by Edison Partners (Aug 2026), bringing total funding to $40M. It connects shippers with spare cargo space on commercial flights and is reportedly profitable with revenue approaching nine figures — real traction, but engineering-hiring signal is thin based on available sources.
assessment.product: An 'infrastructure layer for shipping' — Air Zone Skip, Express Delivery, Express International, and Express Returns products that route parcels via spare capacity on passenger airline flights, then hand off to last-mile carriers (FedEx, USPS, DoorDash, Uber, OnTrac, Veho); sold to retailers, e-commerce platforms, and 3PLs.
assessment.team: Founder/CEO Chris Guggenheim, a 25-year ecommerce/logistics entrepreneur (previously founded X Delivery and ONELIVE, a large Shopify Plus reseller); CTO is Jay Winters. Company reports just under 50 full-time employees plus hundreds of contractors.
assessment.funding: Seed (early 2023), Series A $13.4M (2024), Series B $25M (Aug 2026) led by Edison Partners with returning investors Venture53, Origin Ventures, SaltVC, and SpringTime Ventures; earlier backers included Sky VC (formerly JetBlue Ventures) and Tandem Ventures. Total funding ~$40M.
redFlags: No senior/staff engineering roles found on job boards — only a finance (Controller) opening was identified.
CEO's background is ecommerce/logistics operations, not engineering; technical leadership is a hired CTO rather than a technical co-founder.
greenFlags: Profitable with revenue reportedly tripling year-over-year and approaching nine figures — a real, scaled product, not just a deck.
Moves 30M+ packages annually across a 95-airport network, indicating genuine operational scale.
Raised a Series B (not an oversized seed with no product), suggesting disciplined, evidence-based fundraising.
